metadata.theme: Space travel, Oregon Trail parody, retro-futuristic
metadata.out_the_window_scope: zones, waypoints, events (per-image out_the_window for art direction)

global_style.aesthetic: Modern space art, clean, visually striking
global_style.palette: Deep space blues, purples, cosmic colors, vibrant but not garish
global_style.quality: High detail, professional game art quality

images.content_description: Dramatic view of Uranus from space with a spacecraft approaching. Planet should be prominent, showing its distinctive blue-green color and faint rings. Stars and nebulae in background.
images.text_style: Large, bold, retro sci-fi font, glowing effect
images.mood: Epic, adventurous, humorous undertone
images.notes: This is the main menu screen - make it memorable and inviting

images.content_description: Disabled spacecraft drifting in deep space, emergency lights flickering, debris floating nearby. Distant planets visible but unreachable. Empty space conveys isolation.
images.mood: Loss, dramatic end, but dignified
images.notes: Should feel like 'end of mission' not 'horror' - respectful game over

images.content_description: Spacecraft successfully landed on Uranus surface with colony structures deploying. Uranus's blue-green atmosphere visible above, Earth tiny in the distance. Victory flags or markers planted.
images.mood: Achievement, celebration, pride
images.notes: Player should feel accomplished - this is the win screen

images.style: Generic space station interior or exterior
images.content_description: Generic space station or waypoint view - modular habitat modules connected by corridors, docked spacecraft, supply crates visible. Functional, industrial aesthetic.
images.mood: Neutral, functional, safe harbor
images.notes: Fallback image for shop when no specific waypoint image available

images.content_description: Spacecraft on launch pad or in hangar bay, fully prepped and ready for departure. Chad visible through windows making final preparations. Supplies being loaded, fuel lines connected. Earth visible in background through hangar opening or from orbital platform. Scene conveys readiness and anticipation.
images.mood: Anticipation, preparation, excitement for journey ahead
images.notes: New game setup screen - chad assembled, ship ready, moment before launch

images.content_description: Spacecraft launching from Earth orbit - engines firing with bright exhaust plumes, Earth receding in background, stars emerging into view. Dynamic angle showing acceleration and power. Ship breaking away from Earth's embrace into deep space.
images.mood: Power, determination, point of no return, beginning of epic journey
images.notes: Launch sequence dramatic moment - engines igniting, Earth falling away, journey begins
images.out_the_window: Launch from Earth orbit - engines firing, planet receding, stars ahead

images.content_description: Spacecraft encountering an asteroid field - multiple rocky asteroids of various sizes surrounding the ship, navigation lights on, slight motion blur on asteroids to suggest speed and danger.
images.mood: Tense, exciting, unexpected
images.notes: Generic enough to work for multiple event types - conveys 'something is happening'
images.out_the_window: Whatever the random event depicts—e.g. asteroid field, nebula/signal, solar storm, or derelict; the "something is happening" moment outside the window.

images.content_description: Strange cosmic phenomenon - nebula with unusual patterns, distant unknown signal source glowing, spacecraft instruments lit up. Could be alien artifact, spatial anomaly, or mysterious transmission.
images.mood: Mystery, wonder, slight unease
images.notes: Contrasts with Event-01 - more mysterious than dangerous
images.out_the_window: Whatever the random event depicts—e.g. asteroid field, nebula/signal, solar storm, or derelict; the "something is happening" moment outside the window.

images.content_description: Spacecraft passing Mars orbit (red planet visible in distance), 1/4 journey marker hologram or display showing '25% COMPLETE'. Stars and inner solar system visible.
images.text_style: Large percentage display, holographic or digital readout style
images.mood: Achievement, progress, encouragement
images.notes: First major milestone - should feel like meaningful progress

images.content_description: Spacecraft at asteroid belt / Jupiter region, halfway marker prominent. Jupiter visible in distance if asteroid belt shown. Digital display or hologram showing '50% COMPLETE'.
images.text_style: Large percentage display, holographic or digital readout style
images.mood: Halfway there! Momentum, determination
images.notes: Midpoint celebration - player is halfway to Uranus

images.content_description: Spacecraft approaching Saturn region (Saturn and rings visible in distance), 3/4 journey marker showing '75% COMPLETE'. Almost there - Uranus should be suggested in extreme distance.
images.text_style: Large percentage display, holographic or digital readout style
images.mood: Almost there! Anticipation, final push
images.notes: Final milestone before arrival - should build anticipation

images.content_description: Earth from low orbit, spacecraft in foreground, launch facilities visible on Earth's surface, International Space Station or orbital platform nearby. Blue planet, white clouds, clearly recognizable as home.
images.mood: Beginning of journey, hope, excitement, leaving home
images.notes: Starting point - should feel like 'leaving home' for adventure
images.out_the_window: Earth from low orbit—blue planet, clouds, maybe ISS or launch facilities; "leaving home."

images.content_description: Moon base or lunar station on Moon's surface, Earth visible in the background (smaller), grey lunar surface with craters, spacecraft docked at station. Mix of familiar and alien.
images.mood: First waypoint, progress made, still close to home
images.notes: First waypoint after Earth - nostalgic but adventurous
images.out_the_window: Lunar surface, base or station, Earth small in the sky; first stop.

images.content_description: Mars from orbit or surface base view, red rocky surface, Olympus Mons or Valles Marineris visible, space station or surface habitat, spacecraft refueling. Dusty red atmosphere.
images.mood: Pioneering, frontier town feel, mid-journey progress
images.notes: Classic Mars imagery - red planet, colonial feel
images.out_the_window: Red planet, flyby or approach; Mars base or orbital presence.

images.content_description: Ceres dwarf planet (spherical asteroid) with industrial mining station attached, ore processing facilities, asteroid mining equipment, multiple spacecraft docked. Rocky, cratered surface with industrial structures.
images.mood: Industrial, hardworking, frontier mining town
images.notes: Asteroid belt waypoint - should feel industrial and functional
images.out_the_window: Dwarf planet Ceres and/or asteroid station; belt region.

images.style: Massive scale, gas giant, atmospheric harvesting
images.content_description: Jupiter filling much of frame with Great Red Spot visible, atmospheric harvesting station floating in upper atmosphere, massive gas giant feel, moons visible (Io, Europa, Ganymede). Station should feel tiny against Jupiter's scale.
images.mood: Awe, scale, deep space operations
images.notes: Emphasize Jupiter's massive scale - station should look tiny
images.out_the_window: Jupiter dominant, gas mine or slingshot geometry; gas giant and moons.

images.content_description: Saturn with its iconic rings prominently displayed, station orbiting near rings or Titan moon, golden-brown planet, detailed ring structure with gaps visible. Perhaps Cassini Division visible in rings.
images.mood: Majestic beauty, late-journey checkpoint, anticipation
images.notes: Final major waypoint - Saturn's rings should be stunning
images.out_the_window: Saturn and rings, outpost or station; iconic ringed view.

images.content_description: View from spacecraft window showing Earth filling significant portion of frame, blue atmosphere glow, continents visible, maybe ISS or satellites in view. Still close to home.
images.mood: Beginning journey, leaving home, anticipation
images.notes: Day 1-14 of journey, still very close to Earth
images.out_the_window: Earth still large, Moon nearby; familiar space, "just left."

images.content_description: Earth and Moon both visible from spacecraft, showing their orbital relationship. Earth larger but Moon prominent. Stars in background. Spacecraft solar panels or exterior visible in frame corner.
images.mood: Early journey, exploring near-Earth space
images.notes: Alternate Earth zone view with Moon context
images.out_the_window: Earth still large, Moon nearby; familiar space, "just left."

images.content_description: View looking back at Earth from increasing distance, Earth now smaller but still dominant in frame, spacecraft trail or engine glow visible, stars becoming more prominent. Transition from home.
images.mood: Leaving home, beginning the real journey
images.notes: Further out in Earth zone, transition feel
images.out_the_window: Earth still large, Moon nearby; familiar space, "just left."

images.style: Inner solar system, Mars approach region
images.content_description: Red-tinted space with Mars visible as a small reddish disc in distance, sun brighter and more prominent, fewer stars visible due to sun's brightness. Inner solar system feel.
images.mood: Progress made, heading into inner planets region
images.notes: Day 15-49, Mars region approach
images.out_the_window: Sun/Mars region; inner system, warmer space.

images.style: Inner solar system, between Earth and Mars
images.content_description: View of inner solar system with Sun prominent (but safe to view), Earth now just a bright blue dot, Mars a red dot ahead. Vastness of space between planets emphasized. Asteroid belt beginning to appear.
images.mood: Long journey ahead, emptiness of space
images.notes: Deep inner solar system, transition toward belt
images.out_the_window: Sun/Mars region; inner system, warmer space.

images.content_description: Mars larger now, approaching Mars orbit distance. Phobos or Deimos moons potentially visible. Reddish cast to the view. Mars's polar ice caps visible as white spots.
images.mood: Approaching first major planet milestone
images.notes: Near Mars orbit, transition zone
images.out_the_window: Sun/Mars region; inner system, warmer space.

images.content_description: Multiple asteroids visible at various distances, largest ones showing cratered surfaces in detail. Spacecraft navigating through belt (not dense Hollywood style, but noticeable presence). Grey-brown rocks against black space.
images.mood: Midpoint journey, navigating obstacles, adventure
images.notes: Day 50-77, asteroid belt region
images.out_the_window: Asteroids, Jupiter in the distance; belt and gas giant.

images.content_description: Asteroid belt with Jupiter visible as a large disc in the background, showing it's the target beyond the belt. Large asteroid in foreground showing detail, smaller ones scattered. Jupiter's bands faintly visible.
images.mood: Midpoint, gas giant ahead, progress visible
images.notes: Transition from belt to Jupiter region
images.out_the_window: Asteroids, Jupiter in the distance; belt and gas giant.

images.content_description: View of denser asteroid cluster with Ceres (dwarf planet) visible as spherical body among irregular asteroids. Shows scale difference between Ceres and typical asteroids. Mining operations or markers visible on some asteroids.
images.mood: Midpoint of journey, industrial frontier feel
images.notes: Ceres region of asteroid belt
images.out_the_window: Asteroids, Jupiter in the distance; belt and gas giant.

images.content_description: Jupiter dominating the view, Great Red Spot clearly visible, cloud bands in detail, multiple moons visible as dots (Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto). Spacecraft small against Jupiter's massive scale.
images.mood: Awe at scale, deep in journey, gas giant majesty
images.notes: Day 78-112, Jupiter region
images.out_the_window: Saturn and rings, outer solar system; "past the giants."

images.content_description: Deep space between gas giants. Jupiter now smaller behind spacecraft, Saturn visible ahead but still small. Vastness of outer solar system emphasized. Stars more prominent, sun now just a bright star.
images.mood: Deep space isolation, far from home, determined
images.notes: Deep outer solar system, empty space
images.out_the_window: Saturn and rings, outer solar system; "past the giants."

images.content_description: Saturn visible with rings clearly distinguishable even from distance. Golden-brown planet with ring system showing gaps and structure. Titan moon visible as orange dot. Beautiful but cold view.
images.mood: Late journey, approaching final waypoint, anticipation
images.notes: Approaching Saturn, final major landmark before Uranus
images.out_the_window: Saturn and rings, outer solar system; "past the giants."

images.content_description: Uranus visible as blue-green disc, distinctive tilted axis apparent, faint rings visible if you look closely. Planet growing larger in view. Deep space around it, Saturn now behind spacecraft.
images.mood: Final stretch, destination in sight, anticipation
images.notes: Day 113-140, Uranus approach
images.out_the_window: Uranus growing in the view; blue-green disk, final approach.

images.content_description: Uranus filling significant portion of view, blue-green color prominent, atmospheric bands visible, some moons visible (Titania, Oberon as dots). Planet details becoming clear, approaching orbit.
images.mood: Almost there, final approach, excitement building
images.notes: Very close to destination
images.out_the_window: Uranus growing in the view; blue-green disk, final approach.

images.content_description: Uranus extremely large in frame, spacecraft approaching orbital insertion. Blue-green planet filling most of view, atmospheric features visible, faint rings visible edge-on. Landing approach trajectory visible on instruments.
images.mood: Final moments before arrival, mission nearly complete
images.notes: Final days before victory, orbit insertion phase
images.out_the_window: Uranus growing in the view; blue-green disk, final approach.

images.content_description: View suitable for status screen: Earth prominent with orbital path indicators, holographic displays or UI elements showing mission stats, spacecraft visible with systems highlighted. Professional mission control aesthetic.
images.mood: Mission beginning, organized, prepared
images.notes: Status screen version - more UI/dashboard feel than scenic
images.out_the_window: Earth still large, Moon nearby; familiar space, "just left."
images.interior_focus: Main cockpit establishing shot — introduce the dashboard instruments, personal items, and early-mission readings. Everything fresh and new. Earth visible through viewport.

images.content_description: Earth from orbital perspective with trajectory lines, waypoint markers, fuel indicators, chad stations visible in spacecraft interior. Mix of exterior view and interior systems. Dashboard-style composition.
images.mood: Mission operations, systematic, professional
images.notes: Alternate Earth status view with more UI elements
images.out_the_window: Earth still large, Moon nearby; familiar space, "just left."
images.interior_focus: Navigation and trajectory focus — route displays, waypoint planning, resource gauges. Earth-Moon trajectory plotted. Operational and systematic.

images.content_description: Status view looking at Earth receding, navigation displays showing course to Mars, system readouts, chad preparing for long journey. Mix of nostalgia and determination.
images.mood: Departure, leaving safety, beginning adventure
images.notes: Departure phase status screen
images.out_the_window: Earth still large, Moon nearby; familiar space, "just left."
images.interior_focus: Departure emotion — looking out at receding Earth through the viewport. Navigation showing course to Mars. The transition from home to journey.

images.content_description: Mars visible in status screen with trajectory overlays, system health displays, resource consumption charts, chad stations monitoring approach. Red-tinted dashboard view.
images.mood: Mid-journey monitoring, systems nominal
images.notes: Inner solar system status monitoring
images.out_the_window: Sun/Mars region; inner system, warmer space.
images.interior_focus: Mars-region cockpit — red-tinted dashboard, temperature/heat themes, Mars visible through viewport as approach landmark.

images.content_description: Status screen showing vast distance between Earth (behind) and Mars (ahead), fuel consumption tracking, chad activity schedules, life support systems functioning. Emphasis on journey duration.
images.mood: Long haul, resource management focus
images.notes: Transit phase status screen
images.out_the_window: Sun/Mars region; inner system, warmer space.
images.interior_focus: Resource tracking in transit — fuel consumption, food inventory, systems health. The long haul between Earth and the belt. Duration and endurance themes.

images.content_description: Status screen with Mars larger, orbital mechanics displays, chad preparing for Mars waypoint encounter, resource levels being checked before station arrival.
images.mood: Approaching waypoint, preparation mode
images.notes: Pre-waypoint status check screen
images.out_the_window: Sun/Mars region; inner system, warmer space.
images.interior_focus: Pre-waypoint preparation — Mars growing on sensors, orbital mechanics displays, chad readying for the waypoint encounter.

images.content_description: Status screen showing asteroid tracking radar, collision avoidance systems active, hull integrity monitors, chad at navigation stations. Rocky asteroids visible on sensors and through windows.
images.mood: Active navigation, hazard awareness, focused
images.notes: Asteroid belt navigation status
images.out_the_window: Asteroids, Jupiter in the distance; belt and gas giant.
images.interior_focus: Asteroid navigation systems — proximity radar, collision avoidance displays, hull integrity monitors. Active hazard-awareness cockpit.

images.content_description: Status screen showing Ceres on approach sensors, mining operations in background, resource levels (midpoint check), chad morale indicators, Jupiter visible on long-range sensors.
images.mood: Midpoint journey, resource assessment
images.notes: Midpoint status assessment
images.out_the_window: Asteroids, Jupiter in the distance; belt and gas giant.
images.interior_focus: Midpoint resource assessment — Ceres on approach sensors, supply levels at midpoint check, Jupiter visible on long-range. Logistics and inventory.

images.content_description: Status screen showing asteroid density decreasing, Jupiter looming on sensors, chad reviewing supplies after belt transit, systems check after navigation hazard zone.
images.mood: Clearing hazard zone, approaching gas giant
images.notes: Post-belt status check
images.out_the_window: Asteroids, Jupiter in the distance; belt and gas giant.
images.interior_focus: Post-belt systems check — asteroid density decreasing on sensors, Jupiter looming, chad reviewing supplies after the hazard zone.

images.content_description: Status screen with Jupiter dominating external view, gravity assist calculations on displays, chad monitoring slingshot maneuver, radiation shielding active indicators. Gas giant operations.
images.mood: Complex maneuver, deep space operations
images.notes: Jupiter region status - gravity assist phase
images.out_the_window: Saturn and rings, outer solar system; "past the giants."
images.interior_focus: Gas giant operations — Jupiter dominating external view, gravity assist displays, radiation shielding indicators. Complex maneuver cockpit.

images.content_description: Status screen showing extreme isolation - both Jupiter behind and Saturn ahead visible but distant, chad in routine maintenance mode, life support systems emphasized, resource conservation displays.
images.mood: Isolation, routine, endurance
images.notes: Deep space isolation status
images.out_the_window: Saturn and rings, outer solar system; "past the giants."
images.interior_focus: Deep space isolation — vast distance visible on navigation, routine maintenance mode, life support emphasis. The long quiet stretch.

images.content_description: Status screen with Saturn and rings visible on sensors, final waypoint approach planning, chad preparing for last supply stop, mission timeline showing final leg ahead to Uranus.
images.mood: Final waypoint approach, anticipation
images.notes: Pre-Saturn status check
images.out_the_window: Saturn and rings, outer solar system; "past the giants."
images.interior_focus: Saturn approach preparation — rings visible on sensors, final waypoint planning, mission timeline showing final leg to Uranus.

images.content_description: Status screen with Uranus prominent, orbital insertion calculations on displays, chad preparing for arrival, landing site selection data, mission completion percentage high.
images.mood: Final approach, mission nearly complete, focused
images.notes: Final approach status
images.out_the_window: Uranus growing in the view; blue-green disk, final approach.
images.interior_focus: Final approach instruments — Uranus prominent through viewport, orbital insertion calculations, landing site data. Mission completion percentage high.

images.content_description: Status screen in Uranus orbit, blue-green planet filling external view, chad conducting final systems checks, landing preparations visible, colony deployment equipment ready.
images.mood: Final preparations, excitement, careful
images.notes: Orbital operations status
images.out_the_window: Uranus growing in the view; blue-green disk, final approach.
images.interior_focus: Orbital operations — Uranus filling the viewport, final systems checks, colony deployment equipment readiness displays.

images.content_description: Status screen during landing approach, Uranus surface or upper atmosphere visible, descent trajectory on displays, chad at landing stations, all systems green for final descent.
images.mood: Final moments, mission completion imminent
images.notes: Pre-landing status screen
images.out_the_window: Uranus growing in the view; blue-green disk, final approach.
images.interior_focus: Landing descent — atmosphere or surface visible through viewport, descent trajectory on displays, all systems green for final approach. Maximum energy and activity.

images.content_description: Deep space between Saturn and Uranus, empty void, distant stars, no nearby planets visible, spacecraft alone in vast darkness, perhaps distant nebula or galactic plane. Station beacon or marker barely visible.
images.mood: Isolation, loneliness, deep space, far from everything
images.notes: 75-80% of journey; alone in the void
images.out_the_window: Empty deep space between Saturn and Uranus—distant stars, maybe nebula; alone in the void.

images.content_description: Uranus filling frame with blue-green color, faint rings visible, spacecraft approaching for landing, planet surface or atmosphere details visible, some moons visible as small dots. Final destination achieved.
images.mood: Arrival, accomplishment, relief, excitement
images.notes: 100% - destination reached
images.out_the_window: Uranus filling the view, blue-green disk, maybe rings or moons; final destination.

images.content_description: Solar storm or radiation burst, bright energy waves, spacecraft shields activated, dramatic lighting effects, dangerous but beautiful cosmic phenomenon, chad taking evasive action.
images.mood: Danger, urgency, natural cosmic forces
images.notes: Event variant - solar/radiation hazard
images.out_the_window: Whatever the random event depicts—e.g. asteroid field, nebula/signal, solar storm, or derelict; the "something is happening" moment outside the window.

images.content_description: Derelict spacecraft or station discovered, mysterious ancient or abandoned structure floating in space, opportunity or warning, scanner readings active, investigation decision moment.
images.mood: Mystery, curiosity, unease, discovery
images.notes: Event variant - derelict discovery
images.out_the_window: Whatever the random event depicts—e.g. asteroid field, nebula/signal, solar storm, or derelict; the "something is happening" moment outside the window.

images.style: Relief and celebration — crisis resolved through action
images.content_description: Ship cockpit interior after a successfully resolved crisis. All instrument indicators showing green/nominal. The atmosphere is one of active relief — the danger just passed, the solution just worked. Warning lights that were recently red are now clearing to green. Navigation displays show a clear path ahead. The cockpit shows signs of the crisis that just ended (a tool left out, a panel recently closed) but everything is functioning. The mood is "we just pulled that off."
images.mood: Relief, active triumph, the adrenaline of a crisis just survived
images.notes: Post-event success variant 1 — the "crisis resolved" flavor. Should feel like the moment right after the fix works. Interior cockpit scene, no specific exterior vista.
images.interior_focus: Instruments transitioning from warning to nominal, evidence of recent hands-on crisis resolution, the immediate aftermath energy

images.style: Competence on display — systems repaired, everything working
images.content_description: Ship cockpit interior after successful repair work. Systems that were previously malfunctioning now showing healthy readings. A repaired panel or component visible — the fix is fresh. Engineering tools or repair materials present on the console. All gauges reading nominal. The cockpit feels cleaner, more orderly than during the crisis — someone tidied up after fixing things. The mood is quiet professional satisfaction.
images.mood: Quiet competence, engineering pride, the satisfaction of a good repair
images.notes: Post-event success variant 2 — the "systems repaired" flavor. Should feel like the calm after a successful fix. Interior cockpit scene, no specific exterior vista.
images.interior_focus: Freshly repaired systems, engineering tools, the visible evidence of competent maintenance, instrument readings restored to healthy levels

images.style: Abundance restored — resources secured, supplies replenished
images.content_description: Ship cockpit interior after a successful resource acquisition or resupply. Resource gauges and supply indicators showing improved levels — fuel, food, materials all reading higher than before. New supplies visible through a doorway or on a manifest display. The cockpit feels well-stocked, optimistic. Inventory displays updated with fresh numbers. The mood is the particular satisfaction of being resupplied — not just surviving but being better off than before.
images.mood: Satisfaction, abundance, the comfort of a restocked ship
images.notes: Post-event success variant 3 — the "resources secured" flavor. Should feel like the ship just got a resupply windfall. Interior cockpit scene, no specific exterior vista.
images.interior_focus: Resource gauges at healthy levels, supply inventory displays showing improvement, evidence of fresh provisions, the well-stocked feeling

images.style: Damage taken — systems compromised, warning indicators active
images.content_description: Ship cockpit interior after taking damage. New warning lights active on the dashboard — hull integrity reduced, system alerts visible. A damage assessment readout or diagnostic display showing what went wrong. The cockpit shows physical evidence of the hit: something knocked loose, an indicator cracked, a panel sparking or dimmed. Not catastrophic — the ship is still flying — but clearly hurt. Navigation continues but with new constraints visible.
images.mood: Concern, damage assessment, the weight of a setback absorbed
images.notes: Post-event failure variant 1 — the "damage taken" flavor. Should feel like the ship just absorbed a hit and is assessing. Interior cockpit scene, no specific exterior vista.
images.interior_focus: Fresh warning indicators, damage readouts, physical evidence of impact on cockpit fixtures, systems in degraded-but-functional state

images.style: Resources lost — supplies depleted, operating in scarcity
images.content_description: Ship cockpit interior after losing resources. Supply gauges and resource displays in warning range — fuel lower, food supply reduced, materials depleted. The cockpit feels thinner, less abundant than before. Some systems dimmed or in power-saving mode to conserve energy. Inventory displays showing reduced numbers. The mood is the specific glumness of having less than you did an hour ago — not desperate, but aware of new limits.
images.mood: Loss, scarcity awareness, the glumness of depletion
images.notes: Post-event failure variant 2 — the "resources lost" flavor. Should feel like the ship just got poorer. Interior cockpit scene, no specific exterior vista.
images.interior_focus: Resource gauges in warning range, depleted inventory displays, systems in conservation mode, the visual difference between well-stocked and running-low

images.style: Regrouping — aftermath processed, determined to continue despite setback
images.content_description: Ship cockpit interior mid-recovery from a setback. Warning lights fading from red back toward amber — not fully recovered but stabilizing. Partial repairs visible. The cockpit shows resilience: the chad has addressed the worst of the damage and is pushing forward. Some systems restored, some still compromised. The mood is determination despite bruising — not defeated, just dented. Evidence of both the setback and the recovery effort.
images.mood: Cautious determination, resilience after failure, the resolve to continue
images.notes: Post-event failure variant 3 — the "regrouping" flavor. Should feel like the chad is picking themselves up. Interior cockpit scene, no specific exterior vista.
images.interior_focus: Systems partially restored, repair work in progress, the visual transition from crisis back toward normal operations, determination visible in the instruments

images.style: Earth zone, nightside perspective — auroral light, city glow, familiar-yet-alien
images.content_description: Earth's nightside from orbit — the dark face of the planet lit by aurora borealis ribbons across polar regions and clusters of city lights on the continents. A dramatically different perspective from the daytime Earth views: familiar planet rendered alien and beautiful by darkness. The spacecraft visible in the scene, caught in the aurora's glow. Stars sharp and clear in the unlit sky around the planet's limb.
images.mood: Familiar made strange, nocturnal beauty, intimate view of home from a new angle
images.notes: Earth zone variant offering maximum visual contrast to the daytime departure views in 01-03. The nightside perspective shows Earth as both recognizable and transformed.
images.out_the_window: Earth still large, Moon nearby; familiar space, "just left."

images.style: Ship interior, alternative perspective — a different part of the ship or a different cockpit focus than variants 01-03
images.content_description: Ship interior in the Earth zone — an alternative view from the standard cockpit perspectives. Could be a different room (chad quarters, cargo area, secondary console), a different angle on the main cockpit, or a different instrument cluster in focus. Earth-zone blue light comes through any viewport. The interior should feel fresh and early-journey: well-stocked, personal items recently arranged, everything still new. Distinct from the other earth status variants in composition and emphasis.
images.mood: Mission beginning, fresh start, early-journey domesticity
images.notes: Fourth status variant for earth zone
images.out_the_window: Earth still large, Moon nearby; familiar space, "just left."
images.interior_focus: Alternative interior perspective — different angle, different room, or different instrument focus than earth_01 through earth_03. Early-journey feeling: everything fresh and new.

images.style: Inner zone, solar spectacle — overwhelming natural power, the Sun at its most dramatic
images.content_description: A massive solar prominence arching from the Sun's surface — an enormous curved structure of plasma and energy, dwarfing the spacecraft. The Sun partially in frame as a blazing disc at the image edge, the prominence rendered as a great curving arch of energy. The spacecraft caught in the reflected light, hull blazing with solar illumination. Radiation warnings implied by the intensity. Stars washed out by solar glare. Overwhelming natural scale.
images.mood: Awe at overwhelming natural power, the Sun as both beautiful and dangerous
images.notes: Inner zone variant providing maximum dramatic spectacle. The solar prominence creates a unique composition distinct from the Mars-approach focus of 01-03.
images.out_the_window: Sun/Mars region; inner system, warmer space.

images.style: Ship interior, alternative perspective — inner system heat and light affecting a different part of the ship
images.content_description: Ship interior in the inner solar system zone — an alternative view showing how the inner system's harsh sunlight and heat affect the ship's environment. Mars/Sun region warmth coming through viewports, casting orange-red light. Different interior focus than the other inner variants: could emphasize engineering systems dealing with heat, a different workstation, or how the chad has adapted to the warmer zone. Temperature and solar radiation themes prominent.
images.mood: Inner system heat, systems adaptation, mid-journey operations
images.notes: Fourth status variant for inner zone
images.out_the_window: Sun/Mars region; inner system, warmer space.
images.interior_focus: Alternative inner-zone interior — different angle or room, with inner system warmth (orange-red from Sun/Mars) affecting the environment. Heat management or solar effects visible.

images.style: Belt zone, industrial peak — mining operations at full scale, busy and chaotic
images.content_description: A dense asteroid cluster with full industrial mining operations at peak activity — cranes, ore processors, conveyor systems, habitat pods, floodlights on rocks, multiple spacecraft in a busy work zone. The space equivalent of a highway construction site. The player's spacecraft passing through, dwarfed by the industrial scale. Safety markers and warning buoys between larger asteroids. The belt at its most populated and active.
images.mood: Industrial chaos, the belt as a working frontier, crowded and active
images.notes: Belt zone variant showing the belt's industrial character at maximum activity, contrasting with the navigation-and-transit focus of 01-03.
images.out_the_window: Asteroids, Jupiter in the distance; belt and gas giant.

images.style: Ship interior, alternative perspective — belt zone industrial grey and asteroid proximity in a different interior context
images.content_description: Ship interior in the asteroid belt zone — an alternative view showing belt-zone conditions from a different part of the ship or a different cockpit focus. Grey asteroid light through viewports, industrial belt-region ambiance. Different emphasis than the other belt variants: could focus on navigation/avoidance systems, cargo and supply tracking at the midpoint, or how the chad has settled into the rhythm of belt transit. Proximity to rocks and midpoint-of-journey logistics.
images.mood: Belt navigation, midpoint operations, industrial focus
images.notes: Fourth status variant for belt zone
images.out_the_window: Asteroids, Jupiter in the distance; belt and gas giant.
images.interior_focus: Alternative belt-zone interior — different angle or room, with belt grey filtering through viewports. Midpoint journey logistics or asteroid proximity theme.

images.style: Outer zone, moon gallery — multiple worlds visible, a crowded sky
images.content_description: Multiple outer system moons simultaneously visible — a crowded sky of worlds around Jupiter or Saturn. Several moons at various sizes and distances: some volcanic, some icy, some heavily cratered. A gas giant's atmospheric banding at the frame edge providing warm light. The spacecraft small in the scene, surrounded by moons. The sheer number of worlds in one view conveys the outer system's richness.
images.mood: The solar system's richness revealed, a sky full of worlds, wonder at variety
images.notes: Outer zone variant providing a unique crowded-sky composition distinct from the single-planet or void focus of 01-03.
images.out_the_window: Saturn and rings, outer solar system; "past the giants."

images.style: Ship interior, alternative perspective — outer system void and deep-space isolation visible in a different interior context
images.content_description: Ship interior in the outer solar system zone — an alternative view showing how the deep outer system affects a different part of the ship. Dark void through viewports with Saturn or Jupiter's warm glow as the only external light source. Different focus than the other outer variants: could emphasize communications (signals fading), long-haul endurance, or how the chad has made the interior a home against the void outside. The contrast between warm interior and cold exterior is strongest here.
images.mood: Deep space isolation, warm interior against cold void, long-haul endurance
images.notes: Fourth status variant for outer zone
images.out_the_window: Saturn and rings, outer solar system; "past the giants."
images.interior_focus: Alternative outer-zone interior — different angle or room, with deep space darkness and distant gas giant glow through viewports. Isolation, endurance, or communication themes.

images.style: Uranus zone, top-down ring geometry — dramatic angular perspective, geometric elegance
images.content_description: Uranus viewed from above the ring plane — the planet centered as a smooth disc, rings spreading outward as concentric circles. The geometric precision is striking: a natural bullseye pattern. Moons visible at various ring distances as small dots. The spacecraft approaching on a curving trajectory. The view provides maximum geometric drama and a completely different perspective from the side-approach angles in other Uranus variants.
images.mood: Geometric beauty, a different perspective on the destination, elegant and striking
images.notes: Uranus zone variant providing maximum geometric drama and contrast to the side-view approach shots in 01-03.
images.out_the_window: Uranus growing in the view; blue-green disk, final approach.

images.style: Ship interior, alternative perspective — Uranus teal light flooding a different part of the ship in the final approach
images.content_description: Ship interior in the Uranus zone — an alternative view showing final-approach energy in a different part of the ship or from a different cockpit angle. Uranus's distinctive teal-blue light flooding through viewports. Different focus than the other Uranus variants: could emphasize colony preparation systems, landing checklists, or the accumulation of the entire journey's artifacts visible in one frame. Maximum anticipation energy — the destination is right there.
images.mood: Final approach excitement, preparation, the journey's accumulated story visible
images.notes: Fourth status variant for uranus zone
